P1.evidence: This is a follow-up, so the setter read-back, the four-part frame and the opening discovery question all belong to the first call and drop out of the denominator. What the phase requires on a second call is an agenda and re-agreement, and the rep did both cleanly: he named the purpose up front — 'before we get into the logistic part, which is money, basically' — and then, crucially, checked the value was still intact before touching the money: 'For me, first of all, the most important thing is, do you still feel the same way about the whole program, your goals, and everything?' The answer was 'I do', followed unprompted by the prospect's own reaffirmation that he had shown Trevor's videos to his sister and decided 'this is the guy I want to work with'. That is the right sequencing after a weekend of cold feet.

P2.evidence: Baseline belongs to the first call, which is not in this batch. Nothing in this recording bears on whether age, injuries, health conditions, sleep, diet or energy were ever asked, and it would be wrong to score the rep either way on evidence that does not exist here. Flagged separately for the audit: because the discovery call is missing from the corpus, this closed deal has no verifiable injury or health screening attached to it.

P3.evidence: Goal work was completed on the prior call. The only trace here is the rep's re-confirmation question in P1c and the prospect's own restatement of why he wants it, which was volunteered rather than elicited.

P4.evidence: Past attempts and root cause belong to the first call. Not reachable here.

P5.evidence: Not reachable on a payment call. Worth recording for the coaching file rather than the score: the prospect built his own consequence frame and it was better than anything a rep produced anywhere in this batch — '$6,000 now, as opposed to how many thousands will I have to pay if my health just gets worse, because I need to constantly have medicines or surgeries', supported by his mother's knee reconstruction and his son's $28,000 neonatal stay. The rep's only contribution was to agree with it.

P6.evidence: The gate was held, which is the part that matters — the rep did not open the money conversation until he had reconfirmed the commitment, and he got an unambiguous yes before presenting any option. That satisfies P6c. P6a is partial: 'do you still feel the same way about the whole program, your goals, and everything?' tests continued belief in the programme but is not the scripted question about whether he believes he can get there with the right structure and the right person in his corner. P6b never ran at all — the prospect was never asked whether, if everything were solved, there was any reason he would not go all in. On this particular call the omission cost nothing because the prospect had already answered it voluntarily, but the sequence should not depend on that.

P11.evidence: The most complete Phase 11 in this batch by a distance, and still not finished. Payment was collected live and verified — the financing application was completed on the call, approved ('Oh, I have been approved'), and the first payment confirmed ('it looks like it went through and my first payment was in there'). The Trevor onboarding call was booked properly: the rep checked the time zone, offered real slots, settled on Tuesday 5:15pm Central and had the prospect confirm the calendar email in his inbox during the call. P11c is partial because the rep confirmed the agreement email had arrived and then explicitly declined to have it signed on the call — 'No, no, no. That's the agreement part. You get that covered when you have free time.' The script requires signature on the call, and here payment was taken before anything was executed. P11d is partial because the onboarding form was covered — 'you will have the onboarding form to fill out before the call with Trevor' — but the welcome email was not mentioned and the Skool community link was never raised at all, despite being present in other closes in this corpus.

objection_plays.detail: No think-about-it on this call. The deliberation had already happened — the rep described it in the team meeting as the prospect getting 'cold feet during the weekend' after being sold on Friday — and it resolved off-tape before this recording began. The prospect arrived decided.

No spouse or partner consult; he is divorced and the decision is his alone. There is an adjacent disclosure the rep let pass without comment: he showed Trevor's videos to his sister, who works in physical therapy, and deliberately concealed the price from her — 'I didn't tell her how much it was because she would have been like, absolutely not. Don't do it.' That is a buyer anticipating that the closest informed person in his life would tell him not to do it, and nobody engaged with it.

The play was run through to a resolution and this is the strongest OC execution in the batch. What ran: the value isolate before money ('do you still feel the same way about the whole program, your goals, and everything?'); the no-tough-spot framing almost verbatim from the manager's script ('The last thing I want is to put you in a tough financially spot... And Trevor also doesn't want you to pick whether it's food or training with him'); the invitation to work it out together ('let's have a chat about what's actually possible, and in a reasonable manner for you right now'); and then four of the six financial-picture items — monthly surplus after bills, savings, credit cards, and credit score. The prospect answered all of them in detail and the rep let him talk. What did not run, for the third consecutive call: the permission question, 'are you comfortable having an open, honest conversation about exactly where you're at financially'. Also absent were the 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' frame, available credit per card as opposed to in aggregate, used versus available, and investments. The rep did ask an item not on the scripted list — credit score — and used the answer to route the prospect into a credit product, which is the manager's taught method rather than the playbook's.
No timing objection, despite an obvious one being available to him: he flies to Estonia in five days for three weeks. He never raised it and neither did the rep.
No fear or doubt about the method, the coach or the outcome. He was the most pre-sold prospect in the batch.

Script gap, in a form worth logging. The prospect relayed a credibility challenge from a family member who works professionally in physical therapy: 'she's like, well, I don't know how credible he is where he doesn't want to do bicep curls. She's like, everyone does bicep curls.' He then resolved it entirely himself by explaining the paraphrase had been his own, not Trevor's. The rep said nothing at any point. Third-party clinical scepticism about the training methodology is close cousin to the clinical-fit gap already logged against the Tyron Giuliani call, and here it was handed to the rep pre-resolved and he still did not reinforce it or ask what her actual view was — a physical therapist's endorsement was sitting there unclaimed.

notes: Correct sequencing on a follow-up — reconfirm the value, then open the money — and the fullest financial picture anyone runs in this batch, which is why it closed. Two things to coach: the permission question is still missing three calls running, and the agreement was deferred rather than signed on the call, so payment was collected before anything was executed.
